identity.title: CVE-2026-82663
identity.description: The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.5. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know or discover an existing campaign and team ID to modify the team's name, story, goal, access and notification settings, set its profile image URL, and upload WordPress-allowed media files as parentless attachments. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82568 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: NONE, user interaction: NONE

_relevance.reason: Consumer WordPress plugin with no enterprise or DPI footprint, falls under explicit consumer-only drop class.

identity.title: CVE-2026-82568
identity.description: The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'sort' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Successful exploitation requires the existence of at least one Peer-to-Peer campaign. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82663 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

barriers.summary: network, privileges: NONE, user interaction: NONE

cwe_names.CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

_relevance.reason: Consumer WordPress plugin with no enterprise or DPI footprint, falls under explicit consumer-only drop class.
